factor_scores.evidence_summary: No SELFDESTRUCT in inspected Pendle V2 contracts (ActionAddRemoveLiqV3, router architecture). No audit finding mentioning SELFDESTRUCT in any of 9+ audit engagements.

Router uses diamond-facet pattern where facets are pre-registered (not user-supplied). delegatecall targets are whitelisted facet implementations. No user-controlled delegatecall target found in audits or source inspection.

SY wrappers call protocol-specific underlying contracts (not user-supplied). Router aggregates through registered facets. No audit finding about unfiltered user-controlled call targets in core contracts.

No explicit nonReentrant modifier visible in inspected router action contracts (ActionAddRemoveLiqV3, TokenHelper). Protocol relies on checks-effects-interactions pattern. Penpie exploit (Sept 2024) involved reentrancy in Penpie's code, NOT Pendle core. Multiple audits covered this area without flagging unresolved reentrancy in core.
No ERC-777 integration with unguarded callbacks identified in core Pendle contracts. ERC-721/1155 not part of PT/YT/SY core mechanics. SY standard (EIP-5115) isolates underlying token behavior.

ChainSecurity audit covered arithmetic operations and found no high-severity arithmetic issues. Pendle uses WAD-based math libraries (PMath, MarketMathCore) that enforce scaling before division. No Slither tool run available but audit proxy confirms no divide-before-multiply in pricing paths.

SY standard (EIP-5115) normalizes yield token decimals to 18. PT/YT pricing uses fixed-point WAD math. ChainSecurity audit scope included functional correctness. No mixed-decimal arithmetic finding in any audit.
Spearbit identified and resolved LP truncation issue (syUsed/ptUsed, commit 14c9f26a). No remaining signed/unsigned confusion confirmed in any published audit of deployed code.

No ecrecover usage in core Pendle V2 market/router contracts from inspection. PENDLE token uses governance-based permit pattern (not raw ecrecover in critical path). No audit finding on unguarded ecrecover.

Pendle uses EIP-712 with chainId in domain separator for permit-style calls. No audit finding about missing chainId. Pendle deploys same router address cross-chain via CREATE2 with chain-specific domain context.
Pendle V2 does not use UUPS proxy pattern for core contracts. Router is a diamond-facet pattern. Market Factory V3 is a factory (not UUPS impl). No UUPS pattern identified in deployed core contracts.

VotingEscrowPendleMainchain uses initializer modifier in constructor. Market Factory V3 uses BoringOwnableUpgradeable with Initializable. Router action contracts are diamond facets with no separate initialize() needed. No evidence of unprotected public initialize() on any live implementation. Tree inspection found only PendleCrossChainOracleBaseApp_Init.sol with initialize in name (cross-chain helper, not core market).

VotingEscrowPendleMainchain uses initializer modifier in constructor (functionally equivalent to _disableInitializers() but not the explicit OZ call). No explicit _disableInitializers() call confirmed in inspected contracts. No audit finding about missing _disableInitializers(). Conservative yellow due to partial evidence.

150+ Solidity files across 8+ components. At least 9 distinct audit engagements covering different subsystems. Spearbit 15-day engagement; ChainSecurity at V2 Core level; WatchPug multi-part with follow-ups. Coverage appears commensurate but factory V3-V6 evolution means newer versions may have thinner coverage. Borderline yellow.

[★] sPENDLE governance via Snapshot off-chain. Snapshot takes a block-level snapshot of sPENDLE balances at proposal creation — preventing same-block flash-loan attacks. However, sPENDLE has no hard lock (14-day withdrawal cooldown only), allowing pre-staged whale accumulation. vePENDLE's 2-year lock was stronger flash-loan protection; the Jan 2026 transition materially weakened this posture.

Snapshot quorum not retrievable (JS-rendered). Cannot assess whether a single entity could achieve quorum via token accumulation. Likely yellow given 14-day window for token accumulation against unknown quorum threshold.

Snapshot governance is off-chain and advisory; multisig executes outcomes with no enforced delay. No on-chain governor or timelock constrains execution speed. Multisig could execute a passed Snapshot proposal immediately. [v1-deferred Pass 3]

Pendle documents two supported PT/LP oracle families: the canonical market-derived PYLp TWAP oracle and deterministic Linear Discount Oracles. Chainlink-compatible wrappers can expose selected PT/LP rates to integrators.

The TWAP oracle provides market-derived PT/YT/LP rates; Linear Discount Oracles provide deterministic PT or LP discount paths. A selected Chainlink wrapper fixes its market, duration, and type, so oracle role and fallback remain integration-specific rather than protocol-wide.

Pendle SY adapters wrap heterogeneous external yield sources and expose their exchange rates, deposit and redemption paths. Underlying-yield-protocol failure, depeg, withdrawal limits, or reward-accounting failure can affect the corresponding SY and its Pendle market; permissionless SY and market creation expands the set of integrations that users and external lenders must vet.

The public integration flow requires callers to check and initialize TWAP observation cardinality and wait for a full window; it does not describe an automatic fallback to an independent feed. Linear Discount Oracle is an alternative integration choice, not an automatic runtime fallback for an existing TWAP wrapper.

A failure or depeg in an SY's underlying yield source can reduce exchange-rate or redemption value. Pendle documents a solvency adjustment for asset-denominated TWAP rates and recommends SY-denominated pricing where possible; market-derived TWAP pricing also depends on an initialized observation history. These risks are bounded to the affected market or integration but are material dependency paths.

Pendle's canonical PYLp oracle is a market observation TWAP, not an external spot-DEX read, and official documentation recommends 900 or 1800 seconds. However, the public rate interface accepts duration 0, which reads the current spot implied rate and is explicitly not recommended for production; wrapper duration is selected per deployment.
factor_scores.notes: Critical factor reviewed: no core spot-DEX oracle was identified, but unsafe per-integration zero-duration configuration remains possible.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle recommends 900-second or 1800-second TWAP durations, but duration is selected by the integrator when an oracle wrapper is created. The interface also permits duration 0, so the recommended window is not a protocol-wide enforcement guarantee.

The TWAP rate is calculated from each PendleMarket's observation ring buffer and therefore inherits the market's liquidity and trading conditions. Pendle also allows permissionless market creation; no protocol-wide minimum market-depth control is documented for all oracle consumers.

The canonical TWAP oracle reads the observation ring buffer of the specified Pendle market. It is therefore a per-market source rather than a cross-venue median; deterministic Linear Discount Oracle is an alternative pricing design, not a medianization layer for the TWAP path.

The documented TWAP readiness controls address observation cardinality and age, not price-deviation halting. Deterministic Linear Discount Oracles avoid market-data reads but use a configured linear discount rather than a deviation circuit breaker; no protocol-wide price-deviation breaker is documented for the oracle surfaces.
No protocol-wide price-deviation circuit breaker or corresponding maximum-deviation threshold is documented for the scoped TWAP or deterministic oracle contracts.
factor_scores.notes: not_applicable: a max-deviation threshold is not a parameter of the documented oracle designs.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: TWAP consumers must check getOracleState for sufficient cardinality and an observation old enough for the selected window. For Chainlink-with-quote wrappers, the documentation tells integrators to enforce quote-feed staleness; this is an integration responsibility rather than a universal Pendle-side rejection policy.

The core PYLp and Linear Discount Oracle paths do not require a Pendle-selected Chainlink aggregator. A quote wrapper may use an externally chosen quote feed, but no particular configured feed is in the approved scope for a min/max-bound assessment.
factor_scores.notes: not_applicable: this factor requires a specific configured Chainlink aggregator; optional integration-selected quote feeds are outside this protocol-level finding.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle documents LP pricing as a hypothetical-trade simulation using the market's TWAP-implied rate. No LP-token balanceOf pricing method is part of the documented PYLp oracle design.

Pendle documents LayerZero OFT-based cross-chain PT use and external bridges for PENDLE. Public documentation does not establish a protocol-owned redundant relayer or keeper path for those cross-chain operations, so the external delivery dependency remains a concern.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: MarketMathCore sets MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY to 10^3. On the zero-total-LP branch, addLiquidityCore allocates that amount to protocol reserve and gives the initial provider the remainder, then adds both to total LP. This is an implemented dead-share-style first-depositor guard for the core AMM LP accounting.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: Green: Pendle core LP accounting reserves MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY (10^3) when total LP is zero, preventing the first provider from owning the entire initial LP supply.
factor_scores.notes: Assessment is limited to Pendle core LP accounting; external underlying yield protocols are separately operated protocols.

TN Lee has public professional and recorded-interview trails. The official Pendle paper attributes technical work to Vu Nguyen. These independent public sources provide an accountability surface for named leadership.

Public profiles document TN Lee's Kyber Network history and Vu Nguyen's prior Digix DAO role. Pendle's own March 2021 announcement documents the Benchmark-to-Pendle rebrand. The reviewed sources establish prior protocol involvement but do not claim a comprehensive adverse-history screen for every contributor.

Public explorer pages label the reviewed addresses as Pendle deployment addresses and expose their transaction histories. The public evidence supports an established on-chain history, without making an unsupported conclusion about every historical counterparty or contract.

The reviewed public sources did not establish a protocol-specific prior rug or exit-scam affiliation for the named team members. They are not a complete adverse-history check, so this is evidence-limited rather than a verified clean-history finding.

The public repository exposes a long-lived commit history and contributor listing. It does not establish which contributors held production admin permissions at each relevant merge, so it cannot verify the absence of a short-tenure admin-permissioned contributor.
The reviewed deployer explorer pages do not establish a deployer ENS or NameStone binding. This is an absence-of-binding observation, not a positive or adverse identity conclusion.

Pendle publicly announced the Benchmark-to-Pendle rebrand. The reviewed sources do not provide a complete handle-to-identity mapping for all contributors or a comprehensive cross-project history, so no verified handle-reuse conclusion is made.

The public commit history is available, but this pass did not produce a reproducible contributor-level commit-time analysis tied to independently verified locations. No timezone-consistency conclusion is made.
TN Lee appears in a recorded public interview about Pendle. The reviewed material did not identify a video-off or voice-consistency concern for this named founder.

Public sources provide multiple trails for TN Lee and Vu Nguyen, while some founding-era contributors remain pseudonymous. This pass does not identify all current admin-key holders or support a reproducible protocol-wide OSINT-depth score.

No public, attributable contributor-payment wallet set was available for this assessment. A deployer-address or search-result review is not a substitute for tracing contributor payments to a DPRK-cluster wallet.
factor_scores.notes: Public evidence does not map contributor payments to attributable contributor wallets.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle publicly announced the sPENDLE governance and tokenomics transition, and the public repository exposes an issue tracker. The reviewed public sources do not provide a complete event-to-discussion record for every admin rescue or ACL change, so this factor is evidence-limited and no specific undisclosed-change event is asserted.

Public explorer pages identify the reviewed deployer addresses. This pass did not produce a complete, reproducible 30-day pre-deployment funding trace for every deployment address, so it does not establish a clean or mixer-funded classification.

No complete, attributable three-hop on-chain provenance analysis was available for the deployer set. A keyword search and explorer-label review cannot establish or exclude the factor's DPRK/Lazarus linkage condition.
factor_scores.notes: A complete attributable three-hop provenance analysis was not available from the reviewed public sources.

The public package manifest pins OpenZeppelin 4.9.3, Chainlink 0.8.0, and the listed LayerZero packages to exact versions. No unpinned security-critical dependency is present in the production dependency block.
No malicious-release advisory affecting OZ 4.9.3, Chainlink 0.8.x, or LayerZero packages in trailing 90 days found. OZ 4.9.3 is a stable release.

OZ 4.9.3: GHSA-g4vp-m682-qqmp (ERC2771Context) was PATCHED IN 4.9.3 — this version is the fix. OZ 4.9.4 introduced GHSA-699g-q6qh-q4v8 (Multicall double-execute) but Pendle is on 4.9.3 (unaffected). No high/critical active GHSA advisory for OZ 4.9.3 as used by Pendle.
The public repository and its tags view do not provide signed release tags for deployment verification. The reviewed public materials do not establish a signed release-tag deployment flow.

The cited governanceProxy upgrade occurred on 2025-09-18, outside the rubric's trailing 90-day window for this refresh. No bounded current-window event inventory was produced, so the upgrade count for the required period is not assessed rather than inferred from historical deployment activity.
factor_scores.notes: The available source records a historical upgrade, not a complete on-chain upgrade-event count for the required trailing 90-day window.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No timelock exists (confirmed F032/F033). Any upgrade is structurally a hot-patch without timelock. No specific upgrade confirmed in last 30 days from available data, but the structural architecture permits immediate hot-patching at any time. [v1-deferred Pass 3]
factor_scores.notes: No bounded 30-day on-chain upgrade-event inventory was established for this refresh.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: Partially accepts issue #49 RD-F-139 evidence update. The listed audit directories are added as direct repository sources. No score change is implemented; the row continues to require curator confirmation of exact scope and deployment matching.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: [CRITICAL] Official audit artifacts exist for sPendle, marketV6, and marketV7 in the Pendle repository. The score remains yellow because the correction packet does not prove full current deployed-bytecode coverage for all relevant contracts or fully source the governanceProxy implementation-change concern.
factor_scores.notes: Issue #49: evidence update only, score remains yellow.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No publicly verifiable evidence of a known fix that was merged but remained undeployed was identified. The reviewed public repository and disclosures do not establish the required fix-to-bytecode comparison.
factor_scores.notes: No publicly verifiable merged-fix/deployed-bytecode comparison was established for a known vulnerability.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No test-mode parameters identified. Contracts use production ownership patterns (BoringOwnable with multisig transfers). Router uses production facet routing. No admin=deployer or infinite allowance test patterns found in source.

governanceProxy has undergone 3 implementation changes. Storage layout compatibility not publicly verifiable (no OZ upgrades-plugin output published). sPENDLE proxy also upgradeable. Risk elevated by absence of formal upgrade governance with layout checks.

[★] StakedPendle.sol (implementation of sPENDLE proxy 0x999999999991E178D52Cd95AFd4b00d066664144) calls _disableInitializers() in its constructor. Confirmed from source code at commit 7bde3ec (2026-01-20). Reinitializer attack on the sPENDLE implementation is blocked.

Pendle uses CREATE2 for deterministic cross-chain deployment (same Router address across 6 chains). No selfdestruct in core contracts. CREATE2 redeployment to same address requires selfdestruct first — not present.
The public repository and tags view do not publish a build-artifact hash or signed release-tag flow. The reviewed public materials do not establish reproducible-build documentation.

The cited repository commit date (2026-04-03) is not evidence of a protocol contract deployment within the rubric's trailing 30-day window. No bounded on-chain deployment-event inventory was prepared, so the current-window new-deploy count is not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: No bounded on-chain deployment-event inventory was established for the required trailing 30-day window.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle has a bridge surface: its developer architecture documents LayerZero OFT-based cross-chain PTs, and its application documentation directs PENDLE transfers through multiple external bridge systems.
Pendle documents LayerZero OFT-based cross-chain PTs, but this pass did not verify the active validator/DVN count for each deployed route from a public chain-specific configuration.
factor_scores.notes: A route-specific public on-chain DVN configuration is needed to determine M.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The active LayerZero validator/DVN threshold for each Pendle bridge route was not verified from a public route-specific configuration in this pass.
factor_scores.notes: A route-specific public on-chain DVN configuration is needed to determine k-of-M.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle's public documentation identifies LayerZero OFT and external bridge routes but does not establish validator operator or hosting independence for each active route.
factor_scores.notes: Public route-specific DVN operator and hosting evidence is required for a co-hosting assessment.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The reviewed Pendle LayerZero receive endpoint authenticates the LayerZero endpoint and expected remote sender; the source does not implement an application-local ecrecover verifier, so the unchecked-zero-ecrecover pattern was not found.
factor_scores.notes: Critical factor reviewed: no red finding.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The reviewed Pendle LayerZero receive endpoint validates the expected source chain and trusted remote send endpoint before accepting the message, binding the message path to its configured origin.

The reviewed Pendle receive endpoint accepts the LayerZero nonce parameter but does not maintain its own application-local consumed-nonce mapping. Replay protection therefore depends on the authenticated LayerZero endpoint rather than a second Pendle-side nonce-control layer.

The reviewed Pendle LayerZero receive path authenticates a configured endpoint and remote sender rather than accepting a Merkle root. The default-zero-root acceptance pattern was not found in this application path.
factor_scores.notes: Critical factor reviewed: no red finding.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: This pass did not verify a public route-specific history of validator or DVN rotations for Pendle's active bridge routes.
factor_scores.notes: A public on-chain event review for each active route is required to assess rotation recency.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No public route-specific validator/DVN custody mapping was verified in this pass, so whether one custodian controls more than 30 percent of an active validator set is unknown.
factor_scores.notes: A route-specific public validator/DVN custody mapping is required for this threshold assessment.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle documents cross-chain PT and PENDLE bridge routes, but this pass did not establish route-specific bridged value and active validator/DVN count needed to calculate TVL per validator.
factor_scores.notes: Public route-level bridged-value and validator-set data are required for this ratio.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The known-threat-actor wallet interaction signal requires a current curated threat-actor cluster and recent indexed Pendle contract interactions.
factor_scores.notes: No current public cluster dataset and transaction-monitoring result are bound to this assessment.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Mempool probes by an attributed threat actor require live mempool data and a current threat-actor wallet cluster.
factor_scores.notes: Neither input is available as a reproducible public assessment source.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Malicious-dependency matching requires a complete resolved dependency inventory and an advisory feed matched to deployed or build-critical components.
factor_scores.notes: The public repository does not by itself establish a current deployed dependency exposure.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The typosquat trigger requires a current domain-monitoring feed and verified registration date within the rubric window.
factor_scores.notes: Historical phishing-domain reports cannot prove a current in-window registration signal.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Known-exploit-template deployment detection requires a maintained template corpus and continuous bytecode/selector similarity monitoring.
factor_scores.notes: No current similarity-scan result is available.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Reconnaissance-time estimation requires a labelled peer-protocol incident corpus and attributed attacker-wallet histories.
factor_scores.notes: A defensible yield-tokenization peer distribution is not available from the supplied public sources.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Leaked-credential detection depends on controlled credential-leak and paste-site monitoring that cannot be established from public static sources.
factor_scores.notes: No claim is made about the presence or absence of leaked Pendle credentials.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Identifying a community-channel member as a scam coordinator requires verified moderation or threat-intelligence attribution.
factor_scores.notes: No reliable public attribution dataset is available for this assessment.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle publicly announced the vePENDLE-to-sPENDLE transition, paused new vePENDLE locks on 2026-01-29, and described a two-year expiry for legacy virtual sPENDLE treatment. However, the public materials reviewed do not establish the current asset balance of the deprecated vePENDLE contract, which is necessary to apply this factor's $1,000 and $100,000 thresholds.
factor_scores.notes: The current balance of the deprecated vePENDLE contract was not independently established from public evidence.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The official deployment manifest labels vePENDLE and related contracts as deprecated. The reviewed public sources do not establish that a currently-live admin can reverse a pause on a deprecated surface, nor the economic exposure of any such surface. The specific reversible-pause condition is therefore not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: Deprecated-contract status was verified, but a reversible pause state, live admin authority over that state, and its economic exposure were not established from public sources.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The deployment manifest identifies deprecated contracts, but the reviewed public sources do not quantify active user approvals to a deprecated router or protocol contract. Deprecated status alone does not establish the stale-approval count required by this factor, so it is not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: No public approval scan or allowance dataset quantified active approvals to a deprecated router or protocol contract.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The verified Ethereum Router V4 was compiled with solc 0.8.24. The current public repository config uses solc 0.8.30 with Shanghai and viaIR overrides for router actions. The reviewed compiler sources do not establish a known-bug condition affecting the verified Router V4 deployment.
N/A — Pendle V2 is an original protocol with no audited upstream to compare against for AI-copy risk bytecode similarity detection.

The public repository exposes commit history, but it does not provide a complete, independently verifiable provenance record for every security-critical file. No affirmative AI co-authorship was identified; the absence cannot be conclusively graded green.

No affirmative public disclosure of AI-generated security-critical Solidity was identified in the reviewed Pendle documentation. The public documentation cannot establish that no such disclosure exists elsewhere, so this factor remains an evidence gap.

PENDLE token uses solc 0.7.6 (EOL). However, the PENDLE token is an immutable non-upgradeable ERC-20 — no future security patches needed or possible. All V2 core contracts use 0.8.x (non-EOL, supported). Conservative yellow because token is core infrastructure on an EOL version.

Pendle maintains a live Cantina-triaged public bounty with explicit submission expectations, a $2M total reward, up to $1M critical reward, and scoped Pendle V2 contracts. It also publishes SEAL Safe Harbor contacts and a rescue-report procedure. This is a functional, documented security-disclosure channel, so the factor is green.

The live Cantina program provides submission and safe-harbor procedures but no public acknowledgment or triage timeline. Pendle's public Security page lists audits but does not publish an acknowledgment SLA. Under v1.7.0, a formal bounty without a published acknowledgment SLA is red.

No reviewed public post-mortem or incident record shows a Pendle-core vulnerability previously disclosed to Pendle and then ignored until exploitation. The September 2024 loss was attributed to Penpie's staking/reward logic, not to a known Pendle-core disclosure. Green reflects the absence of public evidence meeting the factor's ignored-disclosure condition.

The public GitHub Security Advisories page for pendle-finance/pendle-core-v2-public reports no published advisories. No open CVE or GHSA against the reviewed Pendle V2 core repository was identified, so the factor is green.

Pendle documents LayerZero OFT-based cross-chain PTs, but the active DVN count, threshold, and operator diversity for each Pendle OFT route were not verified from public chain-specific configuration in this pass.
factor_scores.notes: A public route-specific DVN configuration read is required before assigning a directional DVN-risk score.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Per-market Chainlink-compatible wrappers fix their market, duration and oracle type immutably, but the documented architecture also uses upgradable SY contracts on newer deployments. The reviewed oracle surface is therefore not uniformly immutable across the SY and oracle dependency chain.
factor_scores.notes: Critical factor reviewed: immutable wrapper parameters mitigate individual wrapper substitution, while upgradable SY dependencies keep a material mutable dependency surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Pendle's Market Factory permits permissionless market creation, and its Chainlink-compatible oracle factory permits permissionless wrapper deployment after oracle readiness checks. Pendle does not itself designate every such market as lending collateral, but external lending integrations must validate the market and wrapper they accept.
Security-council threshold-reduction detection requires a defined privileged multisig set, current threshold state, and continuous threshold/timelock event monitoring.
factor_scores.notes: No bound event monitor is available; no current threshold-change conclusion is assigned.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The live Cantina scope explicitly covers the router, seven router facets, core factories, whitelisted SY/PT/YT/Market contracts, and the latest on-chain upgradeable implementations. No explicit exclusion of this approved core surface was identified.

Public reporting describes the Penpie exploit as an attack on an external Pendle integration and separately reports a Pendle social-account compromise. Neither source establishes the specified real-capital social-engineering persona condition; absence of such a report is not proof of absence.

governanceProxy has pause() function (GUARDIAN role) providing chain-level pause capability. No confirmed per-window outflow rate-limiter on LayerZero OFT adapter found. Partial mitigant: pause exists but rate-limiting is not confirmed.

family.description: Yield-tokenization protocol that wraps yield-bearing assets (stETH, weETH, sUSDe, LRTs, etc.) into separately-tradable PT (Principal Token) and YT (Yield Token), plus LP tokens for an integrated AMM with fixed-maturity markets. Also provides an on-chain PT/LP TWAP oracle consumed externally by Aave, Morpho, and Venus for PT collateral pricing.

protocol.description: Yield-tokenization protocol that wraps yield-bearing assets (stETH, weETH, sUSDe, LRTs, etc.) into separately-tradable PT (Principal Token) and YT (Yield Token), plus LP tokens for an integrated AMM with fixed-maturity markets. Also provides an on-chain PT/LP TWAP oracle consumed externally by Aave, Morpho, and Venus for PT collateral pricing.
